what_this_is: The World Machine: observation to state to mechanism to actor response to consequence to conditional future, and then into the United States and the existing New Mexico interfaces.

existing_and_reusable.why: eight machines each carrying variables, relationships, counter_effects, feedback_loops, historical_tests and unknowns
loops with conditions, counter_mechanisms, break conditions and a test — Section W was already built
configuration objects with a selecting condition, a paired opposite and what_would_distinguish_it. Section T existed before the brief asked.
shocks with an entry point and an explicit `not_an_event` field
27 stocks, 34 flows, 8 actor behaviour sets, 5 regimes, 5 substitutions, 15 delays and 4 pressures with `does_not_establish`
the Phase 9 time, geography and correspondence contracts, applied here
the 7D publication contract; both world readings pass through it

existing_but_incomplete.detail: The mechanisms were general and the observations were not. Every loop, shock and configuration could be instantiated for any economy, and all of them were bound to US series.
state_variables existed with a series and a transform, but nothing carried level, direction, velocity, acceleration and percentile as separate things.

existing_but_mis_specified.detail: Phase 9's finding, unchanged: 137 series, all US or New Mexico. Phase 10 does not repair it — it adds a genuinely international register alongside it, and the old one keeps its name and its limitation.

missing: any observation of an economy other than the United States
country state vectors separating level, direction, velocity and acceleration
a configuration comparison that returns similar/different/unknown
accounting discipline refusing unmatched financial claims
a price-quantity decomposition at world scale
executable refusals for the seductive macro inferences
explicit World -> US -> New Mexico transmission

international.contrast: The register named fred_world held 137 series and zero economies outside the United States. This one holds observations for 12 economies that are not the United States.

readings.claim: The major economies are no longer in the same credit cycle: eight are deleveraging and four are not. What is distinctive about China is not that it is adding private debt — Brazil, India and Russia are too — but that it is doing so on roughly twice their stock while its price level has stopped rising, which raises the real burden of the debt it already has without anyone borrowing more.
basis: BIS WS_TC credit to the non-financial sector, 12 economies
BIS WS_DSR debt service ratios, 11 economies
readings.support: Private non-financial credit is rising in four of the twelve economies held — China 204.1% of GDP, India 105.1%, Russia 104.7%, Brazil 92.5% — and falling in the other eight, including the United States (139.7%), Japan (173.7%), the euro area (153.5%) and Canada (218.8%). Of the four rising, China's stock is about double the others' and China alone has a price level that has stopped rising: 0.1%, at the 12.8th percentile of its own history, against 8.7% in Russia and 5.0% in Brazil. US prices are 2.9% and rising.
readings.qualifications: Credit-to-GDP is a ratio of a stock to a flow and its denominator moves with the cycle, so a falling ratio elsewhere can mean rising GDP rather than falling debt. BIS debt service ratios are estimates built from an assumed average maturity and interest rate, not observed payment records. The price series are annual, so no turning point inside a year can be dated. BIS country coverage is not a balanced panel and the euro area is an aggregate of changing membership.
readings.rivals: That the ratio rises because the denominator is weak rather than the numerator strong. This was tested and largely survives the test: China's real output is rising and its price level is near zero, so nominal GDP is growing and a rising ratio requires credit to grow faster still. The denominator is not collapsing. What remains is that annual real GDP and a quarterly credit stock are different frequencies, so the margin is not established precisely.
readings.geography: thirteen economies: the United States, China, the euro area, Japan, India, Germany, the United Kingdom, Korea, Brazil, Saudi Arabia, Russia, Mexico and Canada

requires: the observation is dated, located and attributed
held: the observation is dated, located and attributed
gate.why: the bridge for this rung is held

readings.decisive_unknown: quarterly nominal GDP, which would settle the numerator-denominator question precisely rather than by inference from an annual real series and a near-zero price level
readings.falsifier: quarterly nominal GDP showing the credit numerator flat while the denominator falls would make this a nominal-growth story rather than a credit story
readings.status_means: held evidence supports it and nothing held materially opposes it

currency_bridge.means: close enough that the gap is not material for this claim, and the claim says so
currency_bridge.bridge: The credit and debt-service series run to 2026 quarters; the price and investment series are annual to 2025. The claim is about a configuration that moves over years, and the within-year timing is explicitly outside what an annual register can date.

readings.claim: The clearest single demonstration that a debt stock does not determine a debt burden is inside this evidence: Brazil carries a heavier debt-service burden than China on less than half the stock.
basis: BIS WS_TC credit to the non-financial sector
readings.support: Brazil's private credit is 92.5% of GDP against China's 204.1%, and Brazil's private debt service ratio is 29.8% of income against China's 19.1%. The economy with half the stock carries the heavier burden, because the burden depends on the interest rate and the maturity at which the stock is financed and not on its size.
readings.qualifications: BIS debt service ratios are estimates built from an assumed average maturity and interest rate, not observed payment records, so the comparison is between two estimates rather than two measurements. Country coverage is not a balanced panel.
readings.rivals: The two ratios could differ because of how the BIS estimates maturity in each country rather than because of any real financing difference.

gate.why: the bridge for this rung is held

readings.decisive_unknown: observed debt-service payments rather than BIS estimates of them
readings.falsifier: observed payment records showing the two burdens in the opposite order would remove the demonstration entirely
readings.status_means: held evidence supports it and nothing held materially opposes it

readings.claim: China in 2026 is not Japan in 1998, and the difference is the dimension that matters: Japan had already begun deleveraging by then, and China has not begun.
readings.support: The two configurations are alike on five dimensions — price level, investment rate, manufacturing share, export share and age structure — and differ on private credit, which is rising in China and was already falling in Japan by 1998. The analogy that the price level invites points at the wrong year.
readings.qualifications: Both configurations are reconstructed from CURRENT-vintage data. The World Bank publishes no vintages and revises its back-series, so neither is what was observable at the time, and this comparison cannot establish what anyone would have known in 1998. The dimensions compared are those the register carries, which is not the set someone studying Japan would choose.
readings.rivals: Five matching directions across two economies forty years apart may be coincidence rather than structure; nothing here establishes that these dimensions are the ones that govern an outcome.

gate.why: the bridge for this rung is held

readings.decisive_unknown: whether the dimensions that match are the ones that determine what follows
readings.falsifier: Chinese private credit turning down for several quarters would move it onto Japan's side of the one dimension that currently separates them
readings.status_means: held evidence supports materially different interpretations

interactions.mechanism: Debt is nominal and incomes are nominal. When prices fall, the same debt is a larger claim on a smaller nominal income, so a falling price level raises the real burden of an unchanged stock. Each condition makes the other harder to exit.
evidence: BIS WS_TC private credit 204.1% of GDP, rising
World Bank FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG 0.1%, falling, 12.8th percentile of its own history
interactions.counter_mechanism: Nominal growth from volume rather than price would lower the ratio without any price rise.

interactions.mechanism: An investment rate of 40% of GDP that is falling, alongside a falling manufacturing share, means capital formation is continuing at an exceptional rate into something other than manufacturing. The composition of investment is changing even as its level stays high.
interactions.counter_mechanism: Both shares can fall while absolute manufacturing output rises, because the denominator is growing.

configuration.no_score: A configuration is not scored and not ranked. Collapsing these states to one number would destroy the only thing a configuration is for, which is that they are true at the same time.

selecting_conditions: private credit at its own historical maximum
actor_responses.expected: ease financing conditions to support nominal growth
actor_responses.counter_response: easing into an already-maximal credit stock adds to the quantity whose real burden is the problem
actor_responses.uncertainty: No observation of the policy decision itself is held, so this is the branch the conditions select rather than an observed act

actor_responses.actor: firms outside China buying tradeable goods
actor_responses.counter_response: tariff and trade-restriction policy can close the substitution the price difference invites
evidence: World Bank NE.EXP.GNFS.ZS, China exports share rising
actor_responses.uncertainty: the substitution is a mechanism; no bilateral trade volumes are held to observe it happening

actor_responses.counter_response: deferral lowers demand, which lowers prices further — the response reproduces its own selecting condition
evidence: BIS WS_DSR China private debt service 19.1%, rising
actor_responses.uncertainty: household-level behaviour is not observed; this is the branch the conditions select

orders.claim: The real burden of an unchanged nominal debt stock rises
orders.because: debt is fixed in nominal terms and the nominal income that services it is growing more slowly as prices fall
orders.counter_mechanism: real growth in volume can outrun the price fall

orders.claim: Tradeable goods leave China at falling prices
orders.because: firms facing weak domestic demand and high capacity sell abroad
orders.follows_response: firms redirect output to export markets
evidence: World Bank NE.EXP.GNFS.ZS, exports share rising
orders.counter_mechanism: trade restrictions, which are a policy choice and not a market response

orders.claim: Goods disinflation abroad, and pressure on competing producers abroad
orders.because: the cheaper imported good is both a lower input cost for buyers and a lower price for domestic competitors to match
orders.follows_response: importers substitute toward the cheaper source while domestic producers reprice or lose share
orders.counter_mechanism: a tariff reverses the sign for the buyer and leaves the competing producer protected

refusals.tempting: China's private credit is at 204% of GDP and the highest in its own history, so a debt crisis is imminent.

missing: a debt-SERVICE burden, a borrowing-capacity constraint and a refinancing need
refusal.rule: A true observation is not a valid reading. The bridge is the thing that makes the step, and it has to be held, not assumed.

refusals.what_dula_holds: stock 204.1% of GDP; debt service 19.1% of income and rising
refusals.why_not: A stock is not a burden and a burden is not a constraint. The debt service ratio is held and is not extreme relative to Korea's 19.3% or the United States' own history. Borrowing capacity and refinancing need are not observed at all.

refusals.tempting: China's real GDP is at the 100th percentile of its history, so its productive capacity keeps growing.

missing: a price-quantity decomposition and a productivity observation
refusal.rule: A true observation is not a valid reading. The bridge is the thing that makes the step, and it has to be held, not assumed.

refusals.what_dula_holds: real GDP in constant dollars, and an investment rate of 40.5% that is falling
refusals.why_not: a nominal change with no price-quantity decomposition cannot establish whether output or only its price moved. The World Bank series is already deflated, so the price half is handled; the productivity observation is not held for China.

refusals.tempting: The United States runs a current account deficit of 3.6% of GDP, which shows economic weakness.

missing: what the deficit finances, and on what terms
refusal.rule: A true observation is not a valid reading. The bridge is the thing that makes the step, and it has to be held, not assumed.

refusals.what_dula_holds: the balance, and nothing about what finances it
refusals.why_not: A deficit is an accounting identity with a capital-account counterpart. Whether it is weakness depends on what the inflow buys and on what terms, neither of which is observed.

refusals.tempting: Korea spends 4.9% of GDP on R&D, the most of any economy held, so it has the strongest productive technological capability.

missing: production capability, diffusion or adoption — a knowledge stock is not a capability
refusal.rule: A true observation is not a valid reading. The bridge is the thing that makes the step, and it has to be held, not assumed.

refusals.why_not: Both are knowledge inputs and counts. Production capability, diffusion and adoption are the mobilisation question Phase 9 named, and none of the three is observed for any economy here.

refusals.tempting: Chinese deflation and rising global military spending are both happening, so they interact.

missing: a mechanism by which one condition changes the effect of the other
refusal.rule: A true observation is not a valid reading. The bridge is the thing that makes the step, and it has to be held, not assumed.

refusals.why_not: Dula holds no mechanism by which either changes the effect of the other, so they are recorded as co-occurring and not as an interaction.

transmission.world: Chinese consumer prices at 0.1% and falling, with an export share that is rising
transmission.us_step: US import prices for tradeable goods fall relative to domestically produced substitutes, which lowers goods input costs for US buyers and lowers the price US producers of the same goods can charge
transmission.us_observation_gap: Dula holds no US import price index. The US step is a mechanism with a named quantity and no measurement.
transmission.nm_interface: WE_FREIGHT / construction and food input costs
transmission.nm_landing: UNOBSERVED — Phase 8 recorded that distance from a distribution point is not held by county, so the differential input cost is a mechanism without a local measure
transmission.honest: This chain is representable end to end and measured at neither end of its last two steps.

transmission.world: Global crude benchmarks, set outside the United States by producers including Saudi Arabia and Russia, both of which Dula now observes
world_evidence: FRED DCOILBRENTEU, held in the machines register
transmission.us_step: US wellhead economics in the Permian, which sets production volume on acreage that is partly federal
transmission.us_quantity: oil and gas production on federal acreage
transmission.nm_landing: UNOBSERVED — state revenue reaches the state and no allocation of it to counties exists
transmission.stops_at: state revenue, before it can be traced to any place
transmission.honest: Phase 10 extends this chain's head outside the United States. It does not move its tail.

transmission.world: Fertility is falling in every economy observed here — Korea at 0.7, China at 1.0, Japan at 1.1 — and the 65-and-over share is rising in all thirteen
transmission.us_step: US labour supply through migration, because a world in which every major economy is ageing competes for the same working-age people
transmission.us_quantity: net migration into the US labour force
transmission.us_observation_gap: Dula holds no migration flow series; the mechanism is demographic arithmetic and the flow is not observed
transmission.nm_landing: PARTIALLY OBSERVED — LODES observes who works where inside New Mexico, and nothing observes who arrives from outside it
transmission.honest: This is the weakest of the three. It is included because its weakness is the point: a real world condition with no transmission measurement at any step.

scenarios.name: An energy supply interruption

trace.claim: input costs rise for everything that moves or is heated
trace.because: energy is an input to transport, fertiliser and process heat
trace.counter_mechanism: inventory buffers absorb the first weeks

trace.claim: goods prices rise where energy is a large input share
trace.because: firms facing a higher input cost reprice or compress margin
trace.follows_response: refiners draw inventory; users substitute and reduce discretionary consumption
trace.counter_mechanism: demand destruction lowers the price that caused it

trace.claim: the composition of what is produced and traded shifts toward less energy-intensive activity
trace.because: a sustained relative price change alters what is worth making
trace.follows_response: firms reconfigure product mix and sourcing
trace.counter_mechanism: reconfiguration has a capital cost and a lag, so a short shock passes before the response completes

scenarios.new_configuration: energy constraint added to the existing divergent-credit state
scenarios.qualitative_only: State changes are directional. No magnitude is estimated because no parameter for these mechanisms is held.

scenarios.name: The same energy shock arriving where prices are already falling and debt is at a historical maximum

trace.claim: input costs rise, as in the base scenario
trace.because: the same mechanism; the shock is identical

trace.claim: the effect on the price LEVEL is dampened and the effect on REAL INCOME is amplified
trace.because: where demand is already weak enough to produce falling prices, firms have less ability to pass an input cost through, so more of the shock is absorbed in margin and in household real income than in the price index
trace.follows_response: firms facing weak demand absorb rather than pass through; households already deferring purchases defer more
evidence: BIS WS_DSR private debt service rising
trace.counter_mechanism: an administered or regulated energy price moves the pass-through out of the firm's hands entirely

trace.claim: debt service becomes harder to meet out of a nominal income that did not rise with the cost
trace.because: the shock raised costs without raising the nominal income that services an unchanged nominal debt
trace.follows_response: borrowers prioritise debt service over discretionary spending
trace.counter_mechanism: policy easing can lower the service burden faster than the shock raises costs

scenarios.new_configuration: the same shock produces a different second order because the configuration it lands in is different
scenarios.qualitative_only: State changes are directional. No magnitude is estimated because no parameter for these mechanisms is held.

interaction.claim: The identical shock produces a different second-order effect in a different configuration — dampened in the price level, amplified in real income and debt service.
interaction.mechanism: Pass-through depends on demand. Where demand is weak enough that prices are falling, a cost shock meets less ability to pass through, so it lands on margin and real income instead of on the price index.
interaction.is_not: This is not two shocks added together. It is one shock whose effect is changed by the state it arrives in.

shock_origins.means: arises between states; not an economic cycle phase
shock_origins.why: a supply interruption arises from a decision or an event between states, not from the credit, inventory or capacity mechanisms of the economies it reaches
shock_origins.what_would_make_it_endogenous: if the interruption were caused by underinvestment that the price cycle itself produced, the shock would be the cycle rather than an arrival into it
shock_origins.rule: An exogenous shock may not be read as a phase of an economic cycle, and an endogenous turn may not be excused as bad luck.

shock_origins.means: produced by the economy's own mechanisms — credit, inventory, capacity — and therefore predictable in kind if not in timing
shock_origins.why: a credit contraction is produced by the lending, collateral and debt-service mechanisms the model already holds
shock_origins.rule: An exogenous shock may not be read as a phase of an economic cycle, and an endogenous turn may not be excused as bad luck.

shock_origins.means: arises in a natural system and is not produced by the economy it hits; its timing is not explained by any economic variable
shock_origins.why: hydrology is not produced by the economy it constrains, and its timing is not explained by any economic variable held
shock_origins.rule: An exogenous shock may not be read as a phase of an economic cycle, and an endogenous turn may not be excused as bad luck.

analogue.is_not: CFG_CHN_2026 is not CFG_JPN_1998. A shared direction on some dimensions is evidence about those dimensions and nothing more.
analogue.may_not_be_used_for: a forecast. A historical analogue identifies conditional evidence, not a path.
analogue.why_this_pair: Japan after 1990 is the comparison this evidence invites: a large economy with private credit at a historical maximum and a price level that stopped rising. It was chosen because it is the strongest case against China's position being benign, not because it flatters the reading.

attacks.attack: country selection — is China really the only one?
attacks.result: SUCCEEDED. The first draft claimed China was the only major economy still adding private debt. Brazil, India and Russia are also rising. The claim was false and was rewritten: the split is eight falling and four rising, and what distinguishes China is the combination of twice the stock with a price level that has stopped rising.

attacks.attack: denominator — is the ratio rising because GDP is falling?
attacks.result: FAILED, and the test strengthened the reading. China's real output is rising and its price level is near zero, so nominal GDP is growing and a rising ratio requires credit to grow faster still. The stated rival was tested rather than left standing, and the decisive unknown was narrowed to a frequency mismatch.

attacks.attack: percentile window — is 'its own history' too short to mean anything?
attacks.result: FAILED. The BIS series for China runs 1985-2026, 42 years. The percentile claim survives.

attacks.attack: stock versus burden — does the high stock imply the heavy burden?
attacks.result: PRODUCED A NEW READING. Brazil carries a heavier debt-service burden than China on less than half the stock, which is an internal empirical demonstration of the rule the machine already enforced in code. It is now W3.

attacks.attack: vintage — BIS and the World Bank both revise
attacks.result: STANDS AS A LIMITATION. Neither source publishes vintages here, so no historical reconstruction in this phase can claim to be what was knowable at the time, and each episode says so.

adversarial.outcome: The first reading was wrong in its headline claim and was rewritten rather than defended. One attack strengthened the reading, one produced an additional one, and two stand as recorded limitations.

refuses: No country is scored, ranked or indexed.
No configuration is collapsed to good or bad.
No conditional future carries a magnitude or a probability.
No simultaneous pair becomes an interaction without a mechanism.
No historical analogue becomes a forecast.
No United States series is presented as a world observation.
No Dalio proposition is treated as established because Dalio published it.
